sdf_intersect — 3D sdf_csg op

• Data kinds: sdf × sdf → sdf

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.sdf_intersect(a, b) (to call the implementation directly, import sdf_ops; sdf_ops.sdf_intersect(a, b); from the registry, ops3d.get("sdf_intersect"))

• GPU: none (CPU reference implementation only)

Usage

The intersection of two SDFs, A∩B = the element-wise max(a, b) (inside only where both are inside).

The zero isosurface is the common part of both boundaries. Both inside and outside are generally not strict SDFs, but can be lower bounds of distance.

Calculation: np.maximum(np.asarray(a, float64), np.asarray(b, float64)). per element max, so a point is inside (negative) A∩B only when a < 0 and b < 0. The shape only needs to be broadcast consistent (if not, numpy's ValueError), No other tests will be performed. NaN is propagated, ±inf is strictly propagated (max(a, -inf) = a).

Input: Two SDFs evaluated on the same grid (sphere_sdf / box_sdf / (such as the output of esdf, inner negative and outer positive). The distance unit is the same as the input.

Returns: a float64 of shape after broadcast. <= 0 is the occupation of A∩B.

Attention:

• Outer values can be smaller than the true distance: Outside the intersection, if the point is outside A and outside B When max(a, b) is the distance to the farthest surface,'' the surface of A∩B is further away. There are things (lower bound). The zero isosurface is exact.

• If there is no common part, all elements will be positive (occupancy 0) and no error will occur.

• Used for CSG "cutting" such as cutting a sphere with a box or making a prism with two boxes. Subtracting B from A is sdf_subtract.
